newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's HEW forecasts lower sales in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Germany's HEW forecasts lower sales in 1997.

text.p: German electricity group Hamburgische Electricitaets-Werke AG (HEW) said on Thursday that 1997 turnover would drop because of lower sales and a fall in electricity prices.

This would be offset by cost savings in electricity production as well as lower depreciation costs and payroll costs, management board chairman Manfred Timm said at the group's annual general meeting.
The group said that it was hoping to at least match the good earnings growth of previous years.
In 1996 the group reported record profits of 144 million marks on turnover of 3.96 billion marks.
In the four months from January to April this year turnover was around two percent below that of the same period last year, Timm said.
Electricity sales in the Hamburg region fell 3.3 percent. When the group's total regional electricity distribution was taken into account, the group's total sales grew 1.7 percent in the period.
The group said it had increased its dividend for 1996 to 20 percent from 17 percent.
